editorial: You are dropped right into one of the most tense real-life events of the 1990s. Four terrorists take over an Air France plane in Algiers with 227 passengers on board, and the clock starts ticking. The movie follows the hijackers, the hostages, and the French special forces team preparing to storm the plane. The tone is serious and grounded, with a documentary feel that makes everything feel real. You will feel the pressure building as negotiations drag on and the situation gets worse. The acting is strong across the board, especially from the soldiers who must decide when to act. The pacing is tight, moving between the plane, the command center, and the streets of Algiers without losing focus. On the downside, the movie can feel a bit cold and distant at times, and some characters do not get much depth. Still, if you enjoy true-story thrillers that respect the facts, this one delivers. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the French special forces storm the plane at Marseille airport. The terrorists are killed during the assault, and most hostages survive. The movie ends on a somber note, showing the human cost of the operation and the bravery of the rescue team. There is no big twist, just a realistic and emotional conclusion to a true story.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true-story thrillers and military rescue dramas.
